question_text: Eight employees—Amit, Bina, Chetan, Divya, Esha, Faisal, Gauri, and Hari—are seated around a circular table facing the center. Amit sits third to the left of Esha. Bina sits opposite to Faisal. Chetan is not adjacent to Amit or Esha. Divya sits second to the right of Bina. Gauri sits between Amit and Hari. Faisal is not adjacent to Gauri. Who sits exactly opposite to Chetan?

Six friends—Priya, Qasim, Rohan, Sneha, Tanvi, and Uday—are standing in a row facing north. Rohan is third from the left end. Sneha is immediately to the right of Rohan. Priya stands at one of the ends. Tanvi is not adjacent to Priya or Sneha. Qasim is second from the right end. Who stands between Rohan and Uday?

Seven students—A, B, C, D, E, F, G—attend different classes on different days from Monday to Sunday. A attends class on Wednesday. There are two days between A's and C's classes. B attends class on Saturday. D attends class immediately before E. F does not attend class on Monday or Sunday. G attends class on the day immediately after C. On which day does D attend class?

Five boxes—Red, Blue, Green, Yellow, White—are stacked one above another. The Red box is above the Blue box but below the Yellow box. The Green box is at the top. The White box is not adjacent to the Red box. Exactly two boxes are between the Blue box and the Green box. Which box is at the bottom?

Six persons—M, N, O, P, Q, R—live on different floors of a six-story building (ground floor numbered 1). M lives on an even-numbered floor. N lives exactly two floors above O. P does not live on the topmost or bottommost floor. Q lives on a floor immediately above R. M lives on a higher floor than P but lower than N. On which floor does Q live?

Read the passage:

The gig economy has fundamentally altered traditional employment paradigms. Unlike conventional employment where workers receive steady salaries and benefits, gig workers are classified as independent contractors, trading job security for flexibility. This model has attracted millions who value autonomy over stability. However, critics argue that this arrangement exploits workers by denying them healthcare, retirement benefits, and minimum wage protections. The pandemic accelerated gig economy growth, with delivery and transportation services experiencing unprecedented demand. Companies benefited from reduced overhead costs while workers bore increased health risks without adequate compensation. Recent legislative efforts in some regions have attempted to reclassify gig workers as employees, though industry lobbying has successfully reversed some of these measures. The debate continues over whether gig work represents liberation or exploitation.

Based on the passage, which of the following can be inferred about the gig economy's growth during the pandemic?
option_a: Workers received better compensation during the pandemic
option_b: Companies experienced reduced profitability due to safety measures
option_c: The risk-reward balance shifted unfavorably for workers
option_d: Legislative efforts were more successful during the pandemic
option_e: Traditional employment became less attractive to workers
